plan_a_advantages: More focused on building trail-specific endurance with longer runs.
Includes a second tempo run for sustained speed development.
Incorporates an interval session to improve speed and anaerobic capacity.
plan_b_advantages: More concise and shorter overall duration.
Prioritizes threshold training, which can be beneficial for some runners, though less directly relevant to trail running than overall endurance.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a more balanced approach to building both aerobic base and specific trail-running capabilities. While Plan B includes tempo and hill work, it lacks the consistent, longer endurance runs crucial for trail racing, which are a core component of the goal. Plan A’s longer runs (189 and 104 minutes) directly address the demands of trail distances, and the inclusion of a second tempo run further targets sustained speed. Furthermore, the interval session in Plan A is more directly geared towards improving speed and anaerobic capacity, something vital for a faster runner.
